extraction.name: SWE-rebench
extraction.description: A public dataset comprising over 21,000 interactive Python-based SWE tasks, suitable for reinforcement learning of SWE agents at scale.
extraction.creator: Ibragim Badertdinov, Alexander Golubev, Maksim Nekrashevich, Anton Shevtsov, Simon Karasik, Andrei Andriushchenko, Maria Trofimova, Daria Litvintseva, Boris Yangel
extraction.rai:dataCollection: An automated pipeline comprising four stages: preliminary task collection, automated installation instruction configuration, execution-based installation verification, and quality assessment.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw input data is downloaded from GitHub Archive and GitHub repositories.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The overall patch from a pull request is divided into a solution patch (changes to non-test files) and a test patch (changes to test files).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Issues are linked with pull requests that mention resolving them, and filtered based on criteria such as permissive license, resolved status, merged into main branch, description length, presence of tests, and number of affected files.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: An instruction-following model is fine-tuned using human annotations from SWE-bench Verified to automatically predict three binary quality labels: Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, and Test Patch Correctness.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The fine-tuned model's predictions were evaluated, achieving 81% accuracy for Task Complexity, 67% accuracy for Test Patch Correctness, and 79% accuracy for Issue Clarity.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and benchmark are continuously updated with fresh tasks using the automated pipeline to provide decontaminated evaluations.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset may accelerate the development of autonomous AI systems in software engineering, which brings potential risks such as overreliance on AI-generated code or misuse of automated agents for introducing vulnerabilities.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The fully automated pipeline may result in some tasks being imperfectly described or unsolvable solely from the issue. The initial release is limited exclusively to Python.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and benchmarking LLM-based agents in diverse executable environments, particularly suitable for reinforcement learning.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Our pipeline comprises four stages: preliminary task collection, automated installation instruction configuration, execution-based installation verification, and quality assessment

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: The primary sources for our data are GitHub Archive [Grigorik, 2011] and GitHub.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The primary sources for our data are GitHub Archive [Grigorik, 2011] and GitHub.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: we download approximately 450,000 pull requests linked to issues created before May 1, 2025.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: For each selected pull request, the overall patch is divided into two components: a solution patch, containing changes to non-test files intended to address the issue, and a test patch, comprising only changes to test files.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We then link issues with pull requests that mention resolving them in their title or description, applying filters to select instances where: The issue is from a Python repository with a permissive license. The issue is marked as resolved. The PR is merged into the main branch. The PR is not linked to multiple issues. The issue description is longer than 10 characters. The PR must introduces or modifies tests and includes code changes beyond test files. Changes affect 1 to 15 files.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: To assess these properties automatically, we fine-tune an instruction-following model using human annotations from SWE-bench Verified to predict: Issue Clarity... Task Complexity... Test Patch Correctness.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: For Task Complexity... our fine-tuned model achieved 81% accuracy and a weighted F1-score of 0.82... For Test Patch Correctness... the model achieved 67% accuracy... For Issue Clarity... it achieved 79% accuracy.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: The LLM-generated labels for Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, and Test Patch Correctness are provided as metadata with each task instance.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: We fine-tune Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct using annotations from SWE-bench Verified.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: SWE-rebench uses an automated pipeline from Section 2 for a continuous supply of fresh tasks... continuously updated, decontaminated, and standardized evaluations

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: it may also accelerate the development of increasingly autonomous AI systems in software engineering. This progress brings potential risks, such as overreliance on AI-generated code or misuse of automated agents for introducing vulnerabilities.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: the fully automated pipeline may result in some tasks being imperfectly described or unsolvable solely from the issue... The initial release of SWE-rebench is limited exclusively to Python, restricting its immediate applicability to other language ecosystems.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: designed to train and benchmark agents in diverse executable environments, particularly suitable for reinforcement leaming-based approaches.
